prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset: production sprite atlas for Cosmic: A Sea Beneath the Moon. Input image1 is a STYLE reference only: retain the medallion form, palette, grain and physical depiction approach, but create the NEW requested subjects below. Exactly 4 columns by 4 rows, 16 circles total. Regular equal square cells, Use a SQUARE canvas, exactly 4 columns by 4 rows, equal square cells, no outer margin. Aim2048px wide. Every circle diameter84%of its cell, centred, with generous fully transparent gutters; leave allcells complete and separated. No extra cells or objects. Original astronomical chromolithograph with dry-gouache and chalk masses: deep indigo circular fields, feathered warm-ivory light, amber heat, copper/charcoal minerals and restrained teal water. Simplify to broad meaningful structures visible at72px. Fine grain stays in subjects; generous quiet dark space. One thin ivory circular outline. No glossy UI buttons, photographic lens flare, ornamental decoration, humans, machines, text, labels, numerals, formulas or grid lines. Inside each circle the field is opaque; outside circles true alpha transparency. No shadows, rays or fragments beyond circles. Atom/particle diagrams are schematic: tiny compact ivory dots and diffuse electron-probability clouds, never planetary electron orbits; individual nuclei do NOT glow like stars. Exact invisible chemistry is communicated by game names/readings, never by invented diagnostic coloration. All terrestrial worlds have bare mineral terrain; no plants, life or modern continents. Early Moon is pale gray-ivory without familiar dark maria. All Earth cutaways are views of one continuing world.
Strict row-major subjects (left to right, then top to bottom):
1. Proto-Earth with inherited metal: The same Earth silhouette with a shallow cutaway showing small metallic inclusions distributed through warm rock. Avoid: Inherited metal dispersed, not a completed prefabricated core.
2. A volatile-bearing young Earth: The same cracked young Earth receives one small dark water-bearing asteroid at its upper-right limb. Avoid: No blue surface water or coloured chemical halo; volatile inventory requires label.
3. Theia, a hypothetical rocky embryo: One smaller asymmetrically scarred rocky embryo, cool charcoal facets with a warm lit crescent. Avoid: Use a different rough outline from Earth; no invented known Theia geography.
4. Energy released by accretion: A small rocky body meets the limb of a larger one in one broad amber contact flash with short spreading heat strokes. Avoid: An energy-transfer close-up, not the specific completed Moon-forming impact.
5. Convection in molten silicate: A dark-edged molten-rock cross-section with two broad circulating amber cells, rising centre and sinking margins. Avoid: Rock context with solid crust edge; no arrows masquerading as rigid conveyor belts.
6. Earth’s magma ocean: A close oblique cutaway sector of the established Earth shows orange molten silicate beneath a thin broken charcoal basalt skin. Avoid: One continuing planet; no ocean of water or duplicate planetary bodies.
7. Metal droplets in silicate melt: Several dense copper-gray metal droplets suspended within a broad amber molten-silicate field. Avoid: Surrounding silicate melt is essential; metal droplets do not float freely in space.
8. Sinking and merging metal: In the same amber melt section, descending metallic droplets merge into a broader dense pool at the bottom. Avoid: Visible downward segregation, not an external iron ball inserted into Earth.
9. Earth with an iron-rich core: A generous wedge in the same cracked molten Earth shows one dense copper-gray core beneath an amber silicate mantle. Avoid: One core and one broad mantle, not multiple stellar burning shells or modern continents.
10. Hot melt reaching the surface: A broad amber plume rises beneath a dark crustal edge and spreads sideways near the surface. Avoid: Local cross-section of heat transport, no volcanic gas yet.
11. Crystals in a cooling surface layer: Several angular charcoal mineral crystals grow at the upper margin of an amber melt section. Avoid: Earth's darker crystals remain separate; no continuous crust yet.
12. Fragile rafts of crust: Two irregular charcoal plates float apart on amber lava, narrow glowing channels visible between. Avoid: Separated fragile rafts rather than stable continents or continuous land.
13. Crust returning to the melt: One of the same dark rafts tilts and sinks beneath the amber melt while another remains at the surface. Avoid: Large dark crust slab, not metallic droplets or established modern plate subduction.
14. An oblique encounter: Earth's curved limb and a smaller Theia with one oblique incoming trajectory that grazes off-centre. Avoid: Geometry convention; avoid head-on arrow, numerical angles or already completed collision.
15. Orbits bound to Earth: A cracked molten Earth is encircled by two incomplete elliptical rock paths with sparse debris. Avoid: Closed bound paths as schematic guides, not solid rings or atom orbits.
16. Excess outward speed: One fragment follows a long open outward path past a small Earth, sparse widening motion strokes behind. Avoid: A speed/energy convention, not a jet engine, thrust flame or exact escape trajectory plot.
reference_role: approved pilot style anchor; not a subject/layout template
